text.p: Actor Robert Mitchum, the sleepy-eyed, barrel-chested star of more than 125 films, died in his sleep early on Tuesday, his agent said. He was 79.
International Creative Management agent Jack Gilardi said Mitchum died around 5 a.m. PDT (1200 GMT).
Gilardi said Mitchum died at his home in Santa Barbara, California.
"We've not only lost a great man and a great actor but we've also lost a great friend," Gilardi said.

Mitchum starred in a number of films, including "Ryan's Daughter" (1970), "The Friends of Eddie Coyle" (1973), and "The Big Sleep" (1978) and, in 1983, an ABC television mini-series "The Winds of War," which brought him some of his greatest attention later in his career.
Mitchum had an image in Hollywood as a "bad boy", which was fuelled by a 1948 arrest for marijuana possession that led to six months in a work camp.
